claims.text: Additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components can contain porosity.
Additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components can contain residual stresses.
Additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components can exhibit microstructural inhomogeneity.
Porosity, residual stress, and microstructural inhomogeneity adversely affect dimensional precision and mechanical properties.
Controlled laser remelting reduces internal porosity relative to additive manufacturing without post-processing.
Controlled laser remelting reduces residual stress relative to additive manufacturing without post-processing.
Controlled laser remelting improves dimensional precision relative to additive manufacturing without post-processing.
Controlled laser remelting improves mechanical integrity relative to additive manufacturing without post-processing.
An inert-gas atmosphere prevents oxidation during laser remelting.
Laser power and scan speed must be optimized according to the high-entropy alloy's thermal properties.
Local remelting densifies the material and reduces voids.
Local remelting refines and homogenizes the microstructure.
Local remelting alleviates residual stresses.
Remelting followed by resolidification minimizes porosity and redistributes internal stresses.
A more uniform microstructure sharpens dimensional features.
A more uniform microstructure increases mechanical integrity.
Laser-remelted components will have improved tensile properties and fracture resistance relative to untreated components.
The benefits of laser remelting diminish when initial defect density is excessively high.
Sensitivity of an alloy composition to thermal cycling can limit the effectiveness of laser remelting.
Similar post-processing treatments have reduced defects in other alloy systems.
